To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there are differences between schools in poor areas, that these differences are not captured by the typical context measures, that these differences have a significant impact on school processes, and that the impact of these differences on quality is significant.

the quality problem is partly an artefacts of the inspection system and partly a reflection of contextual effects, but also that there are significant variations in the context of schools in disadvantaged communities and that these are often not reflected in the measures typically used to assess context.

the quality of secondary education in poor areas of Britain is worse than in better off areas, and that the difference is not simply a matter of school performance but of the quality of the schools’ organisation and processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of context and its implications for policy and practice in disadvantaged areas.
the quality of education in disadvantaged areas.
understanding the nature of school quality in disadvantaged areas, the impact of context and how schools respond to this context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
schools in disadvantaged areas face a range of contextual constraints that affect their processes and their quality.
schools in poor areas have to operate within constraints that are not experienced by other schools, and these constraints are not adequately recognised by the school system as it currently operates.
schools in disadvantaged areas are disadvantaged by the context in which they operate, which impacts on their processes and on their ability to provide quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the quality problem of schools in disadvantaged neighbourhoods arises from both internal school factors and contextual factors, but the contextual factors are not adequately recognised in the inspection system, or in the current policy response.
disadvantaged areas have an impact on school quality.
the quality problem is not simply a problem of schools in poor areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
schools in disadvantaged areas need to be supported to be able to do things differently.
the problem of school quality in disadvantaged areas is complex and cannot be addressed by generic school improvement measures.
schools are contextualized organisations.
